citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao (2024). MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. CVPR 2024.
creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao (Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, Nanjing University)
description: MVBench is a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It uses a novel static-to-dynamic method to define temporal-related tasks, and automatically converts public video annotations into multiple-choice QA to evaluate temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). The benchmark covers a wide range of temporal understanding skills from perception to cognition, drawing from 11 public video datasets.
name: MVBench
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An automatic QA generation paradigm was used to convert open-sourced video annotations into multiple-choice QAs. Two approaches were used: (1) Template-Based Construction: option candidates were constructed directly from ground truth annotations (e.g., for Action Antonym: correct action + opposite action + "not sure"; for Moving Direction: four directions + stationary state); (2) LLM-Based Generation: ChatGPT was used to generate questions based on task definitions and to convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format with answer options. For tasks requiring question generation, ChatGPT generated 3 to 5 questions based on task definitions. Ultimately, 200 multiple-choice QA pairs were produced for each of the 20 temporal understanding tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that the multiple-choice format was chosen over open-ended format to avoid biased scoring by LLMs. The paper also notes a minimal source gap between the instruction data used for VideoChat2 and MVBench: CLEVRER in the instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference tasks in MVBench, and videos for Action Antonym are from SthSthV2 while the antonym labels are from PAXION, meaning evaluation is not strictly out-of-domain for these tasks. The paper also notes that longer answer options tend to be correct (answer leakage), which was mitigated by using LLM to ensure similar option lengths.
rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from 11 existing public video benchmarks: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1 (MiT V1), FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. Videos were carefully filtered for diversity, temporal sensitivity (primarily 5s to 35s duration), and question difficulty. Multiple-choice QA pairs were automatically generated from the public video annotations using LLMs (ChatGPT).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations from 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. These cover diverse domains and scenes, ranging from first-person to third-person perspectives, and from indoor to outdoor environments, including both real-world and simulated videos.
rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs struggle with position, count, and character tasks in MVBench. The benchmark reveals that existing MLLMs are far from satisfactory in temporal understanding. The paper notes that visual information alone may not be sufficient for cognition tasks like episodic reasoning (e.g., TVQA reasoning significantly improves with speech subtitles). The benchmark does not include other modalities such as depth and audio. There is a minimal source overlap between the instruction tuning data and MVBench evaluation data (CLEVRER and SthSthV2).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtration was applied based on three criteria: (1) Video Diversity: selection from 11 diverse video datasets covering broad domains and scenes; (2) Temporal Sensitivity: elimination of short clips with negligible motions and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts, selecting videos with intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s; (3) Question Difficulty: for STAR, video clips were randomly shifted at start or end points to increase complexity; for CLEVRER, questions requiring more than 10 conditions were excluded to decrease QA difficulty. Answer options were randomly sampled (3 to 5 options) and shuffled. LLM was used to ensure all answer options have similar and reasonable lengths.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MVBench aims to advance the evaluation of temporal understanding in Multi-modal Large Language Models, which is critical for understanding procedural activities in the realistic world. By providing a comprehensive benchmark, it helps identify gaps in current MLLMs and directs future research toward more robust video understanding systems. The benchmark uses ground-truth video annotations to guarantee evaluation fairness and accuracy, avoiding biased scoring of LLMs.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) across 20 challenging video tasks. The benchmark is intended to comprehensively assess temporal perception and cognition skills of MLLMs in the open world, covering tasks from action recognition and prediction to episodic reasoning and counterfactual inference.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT was used to generate questions for each video based on task definitions, convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format, and ensure answer options have similar lengths. UMT-L/16 (a video foundation model) was used to generate top-6 action predictions as answer candidates for the Fine-grained Action task.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify the number of independent annotations per item; QA generation was automated.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotation was automated using LLMs (ChatGPT); no human annotator demographics are described.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or annotation quality analysis are described; annotation was automated.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform (e.g., MTurk) was used; annotation was automated via ChatGPT and template-based methods.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process.

null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described for MVBench beyond the leaderboard hosted on HuggingFace.
